summary: This note describes the Meydan Mosque, a historical mosque in Kashan, Iran, located on the southern side of Sang-e Ghadimi square beside the Bazaar of Kashan. It is considered one of the oldest structures in the city. Its primary structure possibly dates to the Seljuq era, but it was destroyed during Mongol invasions and later rebuilt and repaired by Khaje Emad ed-Din. An inscription in its old mihrab dates the construction to 623 Hijri (1226 AD) by Hassan ebn-e Arabschah, and the mihrab, which stayed in place until the last century, is now kept in the Museum of Islamic Art in Berlin.
one_line: The Meydan Mosque is one of the oldest historical structures in Kashan, Iran, whose mihrab is now held in Berlin.

The mosque is located on the southern side of the Sang-e Ghadimi square.
The mosque is situated beside the Bazaar of Kashan.
The Meydan mosque is one of the oldest structures in Kashan.

The Mongols destroyed the mosque during their invasions.
The mosque was later rebuilt and repaired by Khaje Emad ed-Din.
An inscription in the old mihrab states that the mosque was built in 623 Hijri (1226 AD).
